solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Air pocket occurring mid-flight?

parts.note: an open shaft of air in a building, around which the flights of steps climb, is an air pocket between flights rather than on an aeroplane

explanation.surface: A passenger's plane hits turbulence partway through the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' means a run of steps, not a journey by air, so the 'air pocket' is the empty vertical space inside a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertical shaft a staircase winds round is a pocket of empty space among the flights of steps.

clue.text: Disappointed with elements switched for arrangement

indicators.note: the two parts of the word are swapped round, the first part moving to the back

parts.note: someone disappointed is upset

explanation.surface: A chemist is let down after swapping the elements in an experimental arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elements' are not chemical ones but the two parts UP and SET, which change places.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-up is the way things are organised or laid out, an arrangement.

clue.text: Relay runner's role as TV presenter

definitions.meaning: the athlete who runs the final, usually strongest, leg of a relay team
the main presenter who links a news broadcast together

explanation.surface: An athlete in a relay team takes on a second job as a television presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both the final runner of a relay team and the main presenter of a news programme.

clue.text: Going backwards, regret road being repaired

indicators.note: something being repaired is being put back together, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A motorist rues a road that keeps getting dug up, which feels like going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrograde describes motion in the reverse direction, moving backwards.

clue.text: Discharges European politician with connections

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament
ties are bonds or links between people

explanation.surface: A well-connected European politician is dismissed from office.
explanation.definitionFit: To empty something is to discharge its contents, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Well-read and inclined to protect leader of rebels

indicators.note: one word protects another by surrounding it, so these letters go round the next piece

parts.note: leaned means tilted or inclined

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A bookish person is minded to shield the head of a rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-read has studied widely and is scholarly, the sense of the adjective pronounced with two syllables.

clue.text: Trip regularly taken by African organisation is a lark

indicators.note: the letters are taken into, and held inside, the organisation's initials

parts.note: the ANC, the African National Congress of South Africa

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word, here the second and third

explanation.surface: A jaunt laid on by an African body turns out to be a bit of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' looks like the jaunt itself, but 'regularly' only picks its alternate letters; 'taken by' puts them inside the organisation's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful caper or prank, which is what a lark is.

clue.text: Eagerly expecting a good turn around

indicators.note: turned around, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Someone waits eagerly for a kind deed to come their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good turn' reads as a kind act, but splits into G (good) and GO (turn), with 'around' turning GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means full of eager anticipation or excited curiosity.

clue.text: Slim girl's first obsession

parts.note: slim means thin

indicators.note: the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A girl's earliest fixation is on being slim.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something is an idiom for being obsessed with it.

clue.text: Soviet official's junior chef — mostly reckless revolutionary

parts.note: a commis is a junior chef in a professional kitchen

indicators.note: something revolving turns round, so the letters are read backwards
most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: rash means reckless

explanation.surface: A Soviet official's kitchen assistant turns out to be a reckless revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts RASH to RAS and 'revolutionary' turns it to SAR; 's is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissar was a Communist Party official in the Soviet Union, responsible for political education and control.

clue.text: Understood Italy to be involved in diplomacy

indicators.note: something involved in another is wrapped up inside it

parts.note: tact is diplomacy or delicacy in dealing with people
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: It is taken as read that Italy will join in the diplomatic talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is understood or implied without being stated openly.

clue.text: Complaints about rejecting cold philosophy

indicators.note: the letters are turned about, rearranged into a new order
a letter is rejected, thrown out of the word's letters before they are rearranged

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about a cold is told to take a philosophical view.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop C from COMPLAINTS to leave OMPLAINTS, then rearrange those nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Platonism is the school of philosophy built on Plato's theory of ideal Forms.

clue.text: No pressure in choices after high school dance campaigns

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: a prom is a formal dance at an American high school

indicators.note: no means that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: options are choices
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Without pressure to choose, a school dance leads on to campaigning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No pressure in choices' removes P from OPTIONS, leaving OTIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotions are publicity drives or marketing campaigns to boost sales.

clue.text: Fruit bugs flit endlessly

indicators.note: without their ends, so each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Insects flit ceaselessly around a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like a surface adverb for constant flitting, but it trims both words.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: The rewards of victory left on board for one who won't enjoy them

parts.note: the spoils are the goods taken by the winners
port is the left side of a ship, facing forward

explanation.surface: The winners' rewards are stowed aboard ship for someone who refuses to enjoy them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' means aboard a ship, where left is port.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport refuses to join in the fun and ruins it for others, someone who won't enjoy things.

clue.text: Arrived with Gunners bearing television equipment

parts.note: came means arrived
RA, the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are called gunners
S, south, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: An artillery unit turns up carrying a TV crew's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like 'carrying' but is a compass direction, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameras are the devices that capture pictures for television broadcasting.

clue.text: People who help with transport of fish and flowers

parts.note: the cod is a food fish
a flower is something that flows, a river

explanation.surface: Helpers carry fish and flowers, like delivery drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' reads as blooms but means things that flow: rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Co-drivers share the driving or navigate, helping to get a vehicle where it is going.

clue.text: Demoralise the papers after case of defence

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: The newspapers undermine a defence lawyer's case.
explanation.definitionFit: To depress someone is to dispirit them and lower their morale.

clue.text: Free starter of tonic — extra ice must be ordered

indicators.note: these letters must be put in a different order
the starter is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A drinker orders a gin and tonic with extra ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as asking for a drink but signals the letters of T and EXTRAICE being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate is to free someone or something from a difficulty or tangle.

clue.text: Misled, but having name for student getting stripped

indicators.note: the word is given a new letter in place of an old one
one letter stands in for another

parts.note: deluded means misled or deceived
L, for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A deceived student is left bare.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L in DELUDED for N.
explanation.definitionFit: Denuded means laid bare, with its covering removed.

clue.text: Inactive worker chasing sleeping accommodation

indicators.note: one chasing comes behind, so this piece goes second

parts.note: a dorm, dormitory, is a shared bedroom
the ant is the crossword's usual worker insect

explanation.surface: A lazy employee follows the others to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means asleep or inactive, temporarily not in action.

clue.text: An indication of complex protein

indicators.note: complex means intricately put together, so these letters are combined in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A biochemist reads a complex protein as a sign of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is a hint or clue, something that indicates.

clue.text: Call the compiler from sound unit

parts.note: to phone is to call
the setter of the crossword refers to themself, me

explanation.surface: Ring the crossword setter from the recording studio.
explanation.definitionFit: A phoneme is the smallest unit of sound that distinguishes one word from another in a language.

clue.text: What cake might be made cold?

definitions.meaning: a cake can be covered in a sugar topping, as a frosted cake is

explanation.surface: A baker wonders how a cake might be chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both covered with sugar topping and chilled with frozen water.

clue.text: Throw out former pupil following exercise

indicators.note: the pupil comes after the exercise

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
PE, physical education
L, a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A school throws out a former pupil after a gym session.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to throw out or eject, as from a school.

clue.text: Help for cleaning up in sweepstake?

definitions.text: Help for cleaning up in sweepstake?

parts.words: Help for cleaning up in sweepstake
parts.note: read the lottery word as sweep plus stake, a stick used for sweeping, a cleaning aid

explanation.surface: Someone hopes for help in cleaning up, winning big, in a betting pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaning up' sounds like a big win, but split 'sweepstake' as sweep plus stake and it is a stick for sweeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled brush for sweeping the floor is a sweeping stick, a cleaning aid.

clue.text: King, left in profit, showed respect

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the letter goes in, inside the next word

parts.note: net profit, what is left after costs

explanation.surface: A monarch who has made a profit bows in respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down on bended knee is a traditional gesture of deference or reverence.

clue.text: Pull up for guard

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: A sentry is ordered to pull himself up.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward can be a guard or protective watch, as in keeping watch and ward.

clue.text: Eased off about scheme for walkway

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the next piece
off means not right, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: Someone relaxed their stance on a scheme for a promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' jumbles the first word into ESADE, and 'about' wraps those letters round the scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a long open level walkway, typically along a seafront.

clue.text: Speak of tariff applied to oranges at source

indicators.note: the piece is attached to, placed in front of, the other
at its source, so the first letter of the word

parts.note: a tariff is a rate charged

explanation.surface: Someone holds forth about a tariff imposed on oranges from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak formally and at length, making a speech.

clue.text: Since returning, youth only eats this!

definitions.text: Since returning, youth only eats this!

indicators.note: coming back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as you're here'
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A young man has come back from somewhere and now lives on leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a returning youth turned vegetarian, eating only greens.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of raw leaves and vegetables is what a youth who has gone vegetarian might eat exclusively.

clue.text: Would it make one patient?

parts.note: patient reads as an adjective meaning tolerant, but as a noun it is one receiving medical care

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what might teach them calm forbearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like the adjective, calm and enduring, but is the noun: receiving medical care makes you a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical care given to someone is what makes them a person under a doctor's care.
